speaker: Unknown
en: Hello, and welcome back to the Cognitive Revolution.
zh: 你好，欢迎回到 Cognitive Revolution。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, my guest is Pete Johnson, a 30-year technology veteran now serving as field CTO of AI at MongoDB.
zh: 今天我的嘉宾是 Pete Johnson,一位拥有 30 年经验的技术老兵，现任 MongoDB 的 AI 方向 Field CTO。

speaker: Unknown
en: We start with a brief history of database technology, going back to the 1970 introduction of SQL, and unpacking how the relative scarcity of disk space at that time informed data normalization as a design principle, and then how decades of Moore's law and the resulting evolution of constraints ultimately led to the creation of MongoDB in 2007.
zh: 我们从数据库技术的简史开始讲起，回溯到 1970 年 SQL 的引入，剖析当时磁盘空间的相对稀缺如何让数据规范化成为一项设计原则，然后再看数十年的摩尔定律以及由此带来的约束条件演变，如何最终促成了 2007 年 MongoDB 的诞生。

speaker: Unknown
en: This history puts today's acceleration into stark relief.
zh: 这段历史让今天的加速显得格外醒目。

speaker: Unknown
en: As Pete recounts, in a remarkably short period of time, we've gone from being effectively forced to implement RAG pipelines by the very limited context windows of GPT-4 class models, to RAG is dead when we first got million token contexts, to the brief token maxing window and subsequent budgetary fallout.
zh: 正如 Pete 所讲述的，在极短的时间里，我们经历了：由于 GPT-4 级别模型的上下文窗口极其有限，大家实际上被迫实现 RAG 管道；到我们第一次获得百万 token 上下文时的“RAG 已死”；再到短暂拉满 token 的窗口期，以及随后的预算冲击。

speaker: Unknown
en: To today, where RAG is again a major enterprise priority, as company data is increasingly available for AI systems to use, usage itself is scaling, and naively maxing out the context window costs multiple dollars each and every time.
zh: 到了今天，RAG 再次成为企业的重大优先事项，因为公司数据越来越可供 AI 系统使用，使用量本身也在不断扩展，而且每一次天真地拉满上下文窗口，都要花上好几美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pete's key point, above all, is that agent performance, and especially cost-adjusted agent performance, depends heavily on effective retrieval.
zh: Pete 最核心的观点是：智能体的性能，尤其是经过成本调整的智能体性能，在很大程度上取决于有效的检索。

speaker: Unknown
en: With this in mind, MongoDB has continued to ship the improvements that developers need to take full advantage of AI.
zh: 有鉴于此，MongoDB 持续推出开发者想要充分利用 AI 所需要的各种改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: Vector search, sorting methods which combine traditional and vector search results into a single result set, a re-rank tool called $Rerank, and their own embedding models powered by the acquisition of Voyage AI, which have some pretty cool features like a shared embedding space across model sizes and a Matryoshka data structure.
zh: 向量搜索、把传统搜索结果和向量搜索结果合并成单一结果集的排序方法、一个名为 $Rerank 的重排序工具，以及他们自己的嵌入模型——得益于对 Voyage AI 的收购——这些模型有一些相当酷的特性，比如跨模型规模的共享嵌入空间，以及 Matryoshka 数据结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: Interestingly, while MongoDB customers are free to use whatever embedding models they like, Pete insists that embeddings are contrary to popular belief, not yet commoditized.
zh: 有

speaker: Unknown
en: From there, we go on to talk about how developers are using these tools to build memory systems.
zh: 从那里开始，我们接着聊开发者如何使用这些工具来构建记忆系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: The write, change, recall, forget loop that Pete sees as the general pattern and why forgetting is currently the hardest part.
zh: 写入、更改、召回、遗忘的循环——这是 Pete 看到的通用模式，以及为什么遗忘是目前最难的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: For now, Pete says it's important to remember that we're only 18 months or so into building AI agents.
zh: 目前，Pete 说，重要的是要记住我们构建 AI 智能体才只有 18 个月左右。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as such, there is no established right answer and nothing like a lamp stack for AI that enterprises can confidently buy and deploy without meaningful customization.
zh: 因此，目前还没有确定的标准答案，也没有类似「AI 版 LAMP 堆栈」那样的东西，能让企业无需进行有意义的定制就放心地购买和部署。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also touch on the lessons he's learned from talking to customers in India, Brazil, Mexico, and Europe all just this year.
zh: 我们还谈到了他仅在今年与印度、巴西、墨西哥和欧洲的客户交流中所吸取的经验教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to my surprise, he reports that the most advanced companies he's spoken to in 2026 were in fact outside of the United States.
zh: 令我惊讶的是，他报告说，他在 2026 年交谈过的最先进的公司实际上都在美国之外。

speaker: Unknown
en: Without further ado, I hope you enjoy this speed run through database history and high-level AI readiness strategy for enterprises.
zh: 闲话少说，希望你喜欢这次对数据库历史的速通，以及面向企业的高层 AI 就绪战略。

zh: 以及对仍在快速演进的智能体记忆前沿的概览。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pete Johnson, field CTO of AI at MongoDB.
zh: Pete Johnson,MongoDB 的 AI 现场 CTO。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome to the cognitive revolution.
zh: 欢迎来到《认知革命》。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks so much for having me, Nathan.
zh: 非常感谢你邀请我，Nathan。

speaker: Unknown
en: I appreciate it.
zh: 我很感激。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm excited for this conversation.
zh: 我对这次对话感到兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been a database guy in the past, and now we're all kind of everything guys these days with our agents greasing the wheels for us.
zh: 我过去是个搞数据库的人，而如今，随着智能体为我们润滑车轮，我们大家都成了什么都搞的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think one of the big themes that we're going to get into is the quality of data is still critically important to making things work.
zh: 但我认为我们将要深入探讨的大主题之一是，数据的质量对于让事情运转起来仍然至关重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm excited to learn everything I can from you over the course of the next hour or so.
zh: 我很期待在接下来大约一个小时的节目中尽可能向你学习一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe just for quick starters, I remember first encountering MongoDB like
zh: 也许先快速开个头，我记得第一次接触 MongoDB 是在

speaker: Unknown
en: 15 years ago, maybe, when a young Guillermo Rauch, who's now the CEO of Vercel, was showing it off in the context of what at that time was like seemingly like crazy futuristic Node.js applications.
zh: 大概 15 年前，当时还很年轻的 Guillermo Rauch——他现在是 Vercel 的 CEO——正在展示它，场景是那些在当时看来简直就是疯狂般未来主义的 Node.js 应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, wow, you can make JavaScript do these kinds of things.
zh: 哇，你居然可以让 JavaScript 做这类事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a way, there's a database that like works in this different way where I'm not constrained by the schema that I already defined.
zh: 而且，有一种方式，有一种数据库以这种不同的方式运作，我不受自己已经定义好的 schema 的约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like this was mind blowing stuff.
zh: 这真是令人震撼的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not sure we've got a lot of technical people in the audience that say AI engineer is kind of our number one profile, but I'm not sure everybody knows kind of the broad lay of the land when it comes to database technology.
zh: 我不确定我们听众里是不是有很多技术人员——他们说 AI 工程师算是我们的头号听众画像，但我不确定每个人都了解数据库技术方面的大致格局。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I thought maybe it would be helpful just to first kind of contextualize SQL versus NoSQL, schema versus schemaless.
zh: 所以我想，也许先简单梳理一下 SQL 与 NoSQL、schema 与 schemaless 的背景脉络会很有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: Give us kind of the high level view so we know where Mongo sits in this obviously bigger database space.
zh: 给我们一个大致的高层次概览,让我们知道 Mongo 在这个显然更大的数据库领域里处于什么位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sure.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I like to think of this in terms of the history, in terms of the different kinds of problems we've had to try to solve with software over the last 60 years or so.
zh: 我喜欢从历史的角度来思考这个问题,也就是从过去大约60年里我们不得不尝试用软件去解决的各种不同问题来看。

speaker: Unknown
en: And where it really starts for me is in June of 1970 is when E.F. Codd, who is an IBM researcher, wrote the original white paper that gave birth to SQL.
zh: 对我来说,真正的起点是1970年6月,当时IBM研究员E.F. Codd撰写了孕育出SQL的原始白皮书。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that was June of 1970.
zh: 所以那是1970年6月。

speaker: Unknown
en: I happen to have been born in February of 1970.
zh: 我恰好出生于1970年2月。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I am as old as SQL, Nathan.
zh: 所以我和SQL一样老,Nathan。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you think about the kinds of applications we were building at the time as an industry and the kinds of hardware we had at our disposal at the time, the applications were very departmental in their nature, right?
zh: 如果你想想我们当时作为一个行业所构建的应用程序的类型,以及我们当时可以使用的硬件类型,这些应用程序在本质上是非常部门化的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Not every company had a computer.
zh: 并不是每家公司都有一台计算机。

speaker: Unknown
en: And those that did, the people that were using it were often on the same floor or certainly in the same building.
zh: 而那些有计算机的公司,使用它的人往往在同一个楼层,或者肯定在同一栋楼里。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were working nine to five hours.
zh: 他们朝九晚五地工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was okay to have downtime on the weekend.
zh: 周末停机是可以接受的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you think about the big three pieces of hardware at the time, memory, compute, and storage, storage was by far the most expensive of those three things in 1970.
zh: 如果你想想当时的三大硬件——内存、计算和存储——在1970年,存储是这三样东西中迄今为止最昂贵的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you think about how you might organize data, keeping in mind that the scarce resource was storage, you would, of course,
zh: 所以,如果你想想你可能如何组织数据,记住稀缺资源是存储,你当然会——

speaker: Unknown
en: Do it in such a way that it's now known as normalization.
zh: 以一种如今被称为规范化的方式来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you may have in university or in coding school, you may have learned things like first and third normal form, all about trying to lay out data on disk in the most efficient way so that you aren't storing any piece of data more than once.
zh: 所以你可能在上大学或在编程学校时,可能学过像第一范式和第三范式这样的东西,都是关于如何以最高效的方式在磁盘上排布数据,从而不会把任何一份数据存储超过一次。

speaker: Unknown
en: The simplest example I can give with that might be my wife and I share an address and maybe with a retailer.
zh: 我能给出的最简单的例子可能是我和我妻子共用一个地址,也许是在某个零售商那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: might want to know what our address is there's two people at that address you might have in one table the list of people in another table you might have the addresses you might have a third table that links the people to the address so these are only storing that address one time
zh: 可能想知道我们的地址是什么,那个地址上有两个人,你可能在一个表里放人员列表,在另一个表里放地址,你可能有一个第三张表把人和地址关联起来,这样那个地址就只存储了一次。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's the most disk-efficient way to do that with, like I said, some kind of normalization.
zh: 而这就是磁盘效率最高的做法,就像我说的,用某种规范化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, fast forward to 2007, which in October of 2007 is when the first commit was made to MongoDB.
zh: 好,快进到2007年,2007年10月是MongoDB第一次提交代码的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the world is a very different place in 2007.
zh: 而2007年的世界是一个非常不同的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: The world has internet.
zh: 世界有了互联网。

speaker: Unknown
en: The world has cloud.
zh: 世界有了云。

speaker: Unknown
en: The world has mobile devices.
zh: 世界有了移动设备。

speaker: Unknown
en: iPhone came out in the US for the first time that year.
zh: 那一年iPhone第一次在美国问世。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a very different world.
zh: 所以那是一个非常不同的世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the scarce resource in that world, because we had
zh: 而那个世界里的稀缺资源,因为我们经历了——

speaker: Unknown
en: 47 years of Moore's law between those two dates.
zh: 这两个日期之间47年的摩尔定律。

speaker: Unknown
en: The scarce resource in that ecosystem became time.
zh: 那个生态系统中的稀缺资源变成了时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because the kinds of applications that we would write that were in the cloud or that we would write for mobile devices, you could not have downtime on the weekends.
zh: 因为我们写的那些在云中的应用程序,或者为移动设备写的应用程序,你不能在周末停机。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was not people who were confined to the same building.
zh: 不再是局限于同一栋楼里的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was not nine to five use cases.
zh: 不再是朝九晚五的使用场景。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was very different world that required a very different kind of database.
zh: 所以那是一个非常不同的世界,需要一种非常不同的数据库。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what gave rise to NoSQL.
zh: 而这就是NoSQL兴起的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now our flavor of NoSQL, which like I said, that first commit was in October of 2007, uses it as its core JSON.
zh: 而我们的那种NoSQL,就像我说的,第一次提交是在2007年10月,它把JSON作为其核心。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you mentioned the stuff with JavaScript.
zh: 所以你提到了JavaScript的那些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why that was so popular 15 years ago or so is because
zh: 这就是为什么它在大约15年前如此流行,因为——

speaker: Unknown
en: What you get back from your API call is JSON.
zh: 你从API调用中返回得到的是JSON。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're storing it in transit as JSON.
zh: 我们在传输中以JSON的形式保存它。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're storing it on disk and a binary form of JSON we call BSON.
zh: 我们在磁盘上以JSON的二进制形式存储它,我们称之为BSON。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's part of why we're so fast is because we're keeping that format the whole time so that when you serialize it off a disk, when it goes through our servers, when it ends up in your client, it's essentially staying in the same format that whole time.
zh: 这也是我们如此快速的部分原因,因为我们始终保持那种格式,所以当你把它从磁盘上序列化出来、当它经过我们的服务器、当它最终到达你的客户端时,它基本上在整个过程中都保持着相同的格式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you think about the kinds of applications that we've been building since 2007, like I said, disk space is no longer the scarce resource.
zh: 所以,如果你想想我们自2007年以来一直在构建的应用程序的类型,就像我说的,磁盘空间不再是稀缺资源。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you take that address example, if you denormalize that data just a little bit, if you, instead of storing it across three tables, if you have a JSON structure that has my name and my address, and then a second one that's got my wife's name and the same address, you're duplicating the address.
zh: 如果你拿那个地址的例子来说,如果你把那个数据稍微反规范化一点,如果你不是把它存储在三张表里,而是有一个包含我的名字和我的地址的JSON结构,然后第二个包含我妻子的名字和相同的地址,你就是在复制那个地址。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what do you get?
zh: 但你得到了什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: In return, what you get in return is one disk read.
zh: 作为回报,你得到的回报是一次磁盘读取。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's why it's faster.
zh: 所以这就是它更快的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: So instead of having to do three disk reads to get that same data, you can now do it in one disk read.
zh: 所以,不用做三次磁盘读取来获取同样的数据,你现在可以用一次磁盘读取来完成。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does that mean that every problem is solved by a NoSQL database or by MongoDB in particular?
zh: 这是否意味着每个问题都由NoSQL数据库,或者特别是由MongoDB来解决?

speaker: Unknown
en: No, but it also doesn't mean that every problem has to be solved with SQL.
zh: 不是,但这也不意味着每个问题都必须用SQL来解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's how that sort of evolved out of SQL was invented at a time where the problems were slightly different.
zh: 而这就是那种演变的方式,SQL是在问题略有不同的那个时代被发明的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of those problems still exist.
zh: 而且很多这类问题依然存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: SQL is certainly a valid solution to lots of different problems that we still have.
zh: SQL 当然是我们仍然面对的许多不同问题的有效解决方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you need speed, when you need scale, and increasingly when you need better retrieval quality, that's really where MongoDB shines.
zh: 但当你需要速度、需要规模,以及越来越多地需要更好的检索质量时,那才是 MongoDB 真正大放异彩的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Reminded of the old saying that the problem has faded, but the solution persists.
zh: 让我想起一句老话:问题已经消退,但解决方案却依然存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's, yeah, see that in a lot of parts of life these days.
zh: 而且,是的,如今在生活的很多方面都能看到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tell me a little bit more, you were just kind of getting to it, but tell me a little bit more about, I mean, Mongo is a pretty big company, $30 billion market cap, obviously has made serious inroads into some of the biggest companies in the world as customers.
zh: 多跟我说一点,你刚刚正要讲到这个,再多讲一些,我是说,Mongo 是一家相当大的公司,市值 300 亿美元,显然已经深入打入了世界上一些最大的公司作为客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: Give me kind of the next level of detail in terms of before the AI moment, and then obviously we'll get into that in depth.
